footprints.description: Same Sky SIM-11-A SIM card socket (push-in, auto eject, card detect), 6 contacts + 2 card-detect pads + 2 shield tabs
footprints.note: sim-11-a.pdf p.3 'Recommended PCB Layout, Top View' (hatched SMT solder areas only; the cross-hatched copper-restricted areas are not pads). Drawing x is from the 'Product center' line, y is up from the product-profile bottom edge (Yb). Contacts C7 C3 C6 C2 C5 C1 left to right: C1 at 3.24 (printed), pitch 1.27 (printed 5-1.27), 1.00 x 3.30 (6-1.00, 6-3.30), Yb 28.00 (printed 6-28.00). CD2/CD1 at 6.66/7.95 left of centre (printed), 0.60 x 2.30 (2-0.60, 2-2.30), Yb 27.50 (printed 2-27.50). Shield tabs x = +/-9.64 (19.28/2), 1.50 x 3.20 (2-1.50, 2-3.20), Yb 3.50 (2-3.50); pin 0 (the pinout names no shield pin). Body = product profile bbox 18.70 (SVG: 139.7 pt / 7.476 pt/mm; page 2 prints 18.70) x 27.55 (page 2 right-hand tab; left part is 25.80), centre at Yb 27.55/2 = 13.775; y_d = 13.775 - Yb. The datasheet's Recommended PCB Layout is a top view with the contact tails at the top and the card entering from the bottom, so every point is rotated 180 degrees about the body centre (x_f = -x_d, y_f = -y_d) to put the card entry at -y.

footprints.description: Same Sky SIM-12-B dual SIM card socket, 2 x 8 contact pads + 4 shield pads

The datasheet's Recommended PCB Layout is a top view with the contact tails at the top and the card entering from the bottom, so every point is rotated 180 degrees about the body centre (x_f = -x_d, y_f = -y_d) to put the card entry at -y.
